items.reasoning: The two missing prompt components are the constraint (two-page limit) and the format (benefits table); the rest are post-hoc or cosmetic.
Generic output traces to context the prompt never supplied, so add audience, hook and events rather than blame capability.
Decompose the multi-part job into ordered, individually checkable stages so a failure is locatable.
Build and verify the dependency everything else rests on first; polish for the client is not a sequencing criterion.
Three functions in one prompt make errors unattributable; separate stages so each returns its own checkable result.
Iterate one component at a time using the flawed output as a diagnostic; wholesale rewrites are why results swung.
Plateaued rewording with invented figures is a missing-input problem: attach the sales data.
Boundary cases are taught by labeled examples, not by more abstract definition.
Constraint level should match task type: tight for analysis, deliberately loose for divergent ideation.
Volatile external facts make this a research-then-draft task; authoritative register is not evidence of currency.
Always evaluate against requirements, source and professional standards; stakes vary the depth, never the reference set.
Accuracy of what is present says nothing about omission; check completeness against what the decision needs.
Accountability is non-delegable: the signer owns every claim, so review to that standard.
Self-reported confidence is not verification; check the two specifics against authoritative sources.
Verify load-bearing claims externally; stated confidence and polish are not evidence.
A systematic framing pattern that survives review means the review criteria are incomplete; add bias and fairness to the routine check.
Volatile, recently revised rules must be supplied or retrieved and then validated; instructing accuracy does not create it.
Request-time grounding = restrict to the pack with citations, plus a licensed 'I don't know'; the fact-check is real but post-hoc, not a prompt provision.
Decision-grade numbers must be computed with code execution, not generated in prose.
A standing review rule turns on stakes/reversibility and audience/regulatory exposure, not on fluency, tier, or deadline pressure.
Mandatory review means a competent reviewer with the source records; a tone skim without the records is not a review.
Verification does not survive a rewrite that changes a claim's strength; preserve claims and re-verify the one that shifted.
Set the criterion before reading so the comparison is not decided by fluency or preference.
Machine-consumed values should arrive as structured data; re-keying prose is the defect's cause.
An evaluation set written by the team does not represent real inputs; rebuild it from messy real contracts.
Non-determinism is inherent, so manage it with a structural review step and a stated consistency bound rather than a defect report.
A safety-critical error is a stop condition; aggregate accuracy cannot absorb it.
Choose the surface from the task's shape first; recurring context-heavy work is what Projects exist for.
Current information across many external sources is exactly the research-mode fit.
A twice-a-quarter reviewed task does not justify agentic automation; match the surface to frequency and stakes.
Repeatable procedure = Skill; verifiably correct totals = code execution.
Tier ladder maps to workload: light tier for high-volume extraction, mid for everyday work, top for hard strategy.
When both tiers clear the quality bar and the optimization target is speed and cost, take the cheapest that clears.
Top-tier-for-everything is a cost and latency anti-pattern; right-size routing per workload.
Week-long thread degradation is context-window exhaustion, not model regression.
Carry the durable conclusions into a fresh session proactively, before context pressure degrades quality.
Context window is within-conversation; Memory is the cross-session persistence layer — that split explains both observations.
Best use is structured, source-traceable, testable requirements the team can act on, not a readable gist or a whole process design.
Verifiability before downstream consumption is the delegation criterion; repetitiveness and confident tone are not.
Compute the figures from the export with code execution and let the model synthesize around them.
Measure the workflow before delegating; intuition about the biggest time sink is unverified.
Stage checkpoints are where human judgment re-enters; strong drafts are not a reason to remove them.
Change only the component the review indicted; keep what passed.
Automate the reversible steps and keep the human approval gate before the irreversible commitment.
Classify each step on reversibility, stakes and accountability into a three-way verdict, not a binary.
A real gate sits before the irreversible act and has a named accountable owner; post-hoc logs and timeout auto-clears are not gates.
A fixed-sequence, checklist-validated process is a structured workflow; autonomy adds risk without adding capability.
Build the simplest design that meets the stated requirement; the scoring pipeline is unrequested complexity.
Durable trust comes from capabilities stated with their limits plus the review gates that make them safe.
Deliver what is in scope and escalate the API build to the Developer role; scope boundary, not credential sharing.
Recurring work amortizes configuration cost; the afternoon pays back on every later run.
Right layer for each artifact: reference data in knowledge, procedure as a Skill, instructions for behavior.
Repeated failure on an out-of-scope action is a capability-edge problem no rewording fixes.
Curate before uploading: screen for authority and currency with a recorded owner, and scope to actual need with a refresh cadence.
Conflicting knowledge needs explicit precedence by scope, surfaced in the reply; retrieval order is not a policy.
Upload recency is not content currency; verify against the agency's current rules.
Unobservable, untestable instructions do nothing; rewrite as precise rules whose effect can be seen in a draft.
Durable rules belong in instructions; uploaded files are data and carry no instruction authority.
Configuration decay is silent, so it must be caught by a scheduled review rather than by complaints.
A shared configuration change has downstream consumers who must be told what changed.
Screening is a graded judgment on reversibility, consequence, human element and accountability, not a yes/no gate.
Policy sets boundaries, not answers; judge the uncovered case against those boundaries and record the reasoning.
Classify the data against policy, then match handling to the classification (de-identify and scope); an instruction line is not a control.
The restriction attaches to the regulated identifiers, so redact them and summarize the permitted narrative.
The deciding question is where data comes to rest per surface: retention, Memory persistence and connector scope.
Minimize what is logged and retain only as long as policy allows; access control does not fix indefinite retention of identifiers.
Deadline pressure and local risk arguments do not authorize a bypass; take a documented exception to the policy owner.
A community Skill is third-party software: evaluate provenance and requested permissions before enabling.
Model changes are evaluated against a baseline on the team's own work, then staged; neither auto-adopt nor freeze.
Hold the boundary while preserving the relationship: name it, offer the permitted alternative, log the escalation.
Ambiguity is resolved by reasoning through the screening criteria and recording the verdict, not by instinct or precedent elsewhere.
A decision communicated to an affected person owes disclosure of AI involvement and a route to contest.
Work the diagnostic layers in order before escalating to tier changes or vendor tickets.
The fix follows from the diagnosis: identify which layer failed rather than pattern-matching a past fix.
Consistently strong drafts needing an edit is an expectation mismatch, not a prompt or tier defect.
Three simultaneous changes are unattributable; re-baseline and reintroduce them one at a time.
A new refusal on changed inputs is a policy/permission signal: check task, policy and permissions, then redo the permitted part.
Convert vague feedback into one specific, named change to the request.
Institutionalize the working fix in the Project instructions or a Skill so it is the default for everyone.
A checkable gain needs a reconstructed before measure and the same measures after, on an instrumented workflow.
